newsitem.title: USA: Explosion rocks Atlanta gay and lesbian nightclub.
newsitem.headline: Explosion rocks Atlanta gay and lesbian nightclub.

text.p: An explosion rocked a crowded gay and lesbian nightclub in Atlanta late on Friday, leaving at least two people injured, police said.

The blast occurred at about 10 p.m. EST outside a building housing the Otherside Lounge of Atlanta. Police said the injured were taken to a nearby hospital but could not confirm local press reports saying a man and a woman had been hit by flying nails.
Authorities also could not say immediately whether the blast had been caused by a bomb. No warning call preceded the explosion.
Explosives experts from the Atlanta city police bomb squad, the FBI and the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms descended on the site and began searching the area for evidence of a bomb.
"At this time, we don't know what type of device it was," Atlanta Police Sgt. J.L. Montgomery said.
One witness, a fireman on duty at a neighbourhood fire house, said the blast sounded like an electrical transformer exploding.
The nightclub was located in the city's Buckhead neighbourhood, a centre of weekend night life.

A month ago, two bombs exploded at an Atlanta abortion clinic, injuring half a dozen people. The first bomb, placed just outside the clinic office, shattered the first floor of the building. Police believe the second device, hidden in a corner of the parking lot, was intended for law enforcement agents who responded to the initial emergency call.
Last July, a powerful pipe bomb exploded in downtown Atlanta during the Summer Olympics, leaving two people dead and more than 100 injured.
